text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Parliament expresses regret over attempts by Singapore Democratic Party to mislead Singaporeans over isuse of government subsidy in health care.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong suggests on Netherlands visit that Dutch draw up scheme whereby countries' transhipment centres actively interact with one another.
- Malaysia Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad breaks down and weeps at opening of Umno General Assembly when asking Umno delegates to reject bribes.
- Three controlling shareholders of Causeway Investment Ltd sell combined 13.19 percent stake of 9.82 million shares at Singapore $1.70 per share.
- Five adjacent residential properties up for tender after provisional permission to redevelop sites secured.
- China-based NatSteel Broadway Ltd becomes third initial public offering to close below its offer price.
- Hoteliers brace themselves for tough year ahead with an oversupply of rooms.
- Malaysia's Education Minister Najob Tun Razak wins in Umno General Assembly that will put him on track for future deputy Prime Minister post.
- Forum The Shopping Mall may be redeveloped into 30-storey complex.
- Property stocks fall on news of low interest in government tender for downtown commercial land.
- Hong Leong group's New Zealand property investment arm, CDL Investments New Zealand, sells an Auckland property.
